report:
**Conclusion:** The evidence partially supports your view but needs nuance. Dexamethasone does not *guarantee* survival, but for critically ill COVID-19 patients (those needing oxygen or ventilation), it does significantly improve survival odds. It does not benefit—and may harm—patients who do not require respiratory support.

**Evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY trial (NEJM, 2021):** In hospitalized COVID-19 patients, dexamethasone (6 mg/day for up to 10 days) lowered 28-day mortality among those receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (29.3% vs. 41.4% with usual care) and among those receiving oxygen alone (23.3% vs. 26.2%). However, there was no benefit in patients not receiving respiratory support.  
   https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436

2. **WHO living guideline (2020):** WHO issued a *strong recommendation* for systemic corticosteroids in severe and critical COVID-19, citing moderate-certainty evidence of lower mortality. It gave a *conditional recommendation against* corticosteroids in non-severe cases.  
   https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-2019-nCoV-Corticosteroids-2020.1

3. **Meta-analysis (NEJM Evidence, 2023):** Glucocorticoids likely *increase* mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients not receiving oxygen (number needed to harm = 27), reinforcing that benefit is limited to severe/critical illness.  
   https://evidence.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/EVIDoa2200283

4. **Observational study (Springer, 2024):** Dexamethasone was associated with reduced both 28-day and 1-year mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients, especially those on non-invasive or invasive ventilation.  
   https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12879-024-10216-3

**Bottom line:** Dexamethasone does not "ensure" survival, but it does meaningfully reduce mortality in critically ill COVID-19 patients requiring oxygen or ventilation. It provides no benefit and may cause harm in milder cases without oxygen needs.
